title: Three algal samples
body: A student collected three algal samples and recorded these observations. Sample P, from a pond, is grass green; its chloroplasts contain pyrenoids with protein besides starch, its cell wall has an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose, and its zoospores bear 2 to 8 equal, apical flagella. Sample Q, from the sea, is olive brown; its body is attached to a rock by a holdfast and has a stalk-like stipe and a leaf-like frond; its cell wall is covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating, and its zoospores are pear-shaped with two unequal, laterally attached flagella. Sample R, dredged from a great depth in a warm sea, is red; no flagellated cell was seen at any stage of its life cycle, and its stored food is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
